record.original_question: For holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler manifolds whose leaves have dimension greater than 1, what is the correct replacement for directed ddc-closed currents of bi-dimension (1,1) used in the one-dimensional case, so that one can develop an ergodic theory for such foliations?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.1. In order to study foliations with leaves of dimension larger than 1, what is the right notion which substitutes directed ddc-closed currents in dimension 1 that should be considered ? Such objects should permit to develop the ergodic theory for these foliations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a (possibly singular) holomorphic foliation on $X$ whose leaves have complex dimension $k > 1$. In the case $k=1$ (foliations by Riemann surfaces), the ergodic theory of $\mathcal{F}$ is built on the notion of a positive $dd^c$-closed current of bi-dimension $(1,1)$ directed by $\mathcal{F}$, i.e. a positive current $T$ on $X$ of bi-dimension $(1,1)$ such that $dd^c T = 0$ and such that, in flow boxes, $T$ is an average of integration currents along the local plaques against a transverse positive measure.

Problem: Identify the correct higher-dimensional analogue of such directed $dd^c$-closed $(1,1)$-currents for foliations with leaves of dimension $k>1$. More precisely, define a class of positive currents on $X$ associated to $\mathcal{F}$ — playing for $k$-dimensional leaves the same role that directed positive $dd^c$-closed $(1,1)$-currents play for $1$-dimensional leaves — such that this class supports the development of an ergodic theory (existence, uniqueness, and ergodic theorems for averages along leaves) for holomorphic foliations of leaf dimension greater than $1$ on compact Kähler manifolds.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on ergodic theory of holomorphic foliations (e.g., works on directed harmonic and $dd^c$-closed currents, unique ergodicity results on Kähler surfaces) focus on the leaf-dimension-one case (foliations by Riemann surfaces). No accepted definitive substitute notion has been established for leaves of dimension greater than one; the question of the correct directed-current object for higher-dimensional leaves appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic theorems for laminations and foliations: recent results and perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: Central notions include leafwise Poincaré metric, directed positive harmonic currents... for singular holomorphic foliations by curves.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys frame the ergodic theory of holomorphic foliations around directed currents for leaf dimension 1, with the higher-dimensional analogue not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Unique Ergodicity for foliations on compact Kähler surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Unique positive ddc-closed (1,1)-current directed by the foliation on compact Kähler surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art unique ergodicity results remain in the leaf-dimension-one setting using directed ddc-closed (1,1)-currents.
